rationale: Two small, honest corrections after the membership thread resolved. First, a consistency fix: the removed-member question d82592dffc9d4a5893fbc6028fc438e7-question-0 has a final refuting interpretation but is still marked active, so its disposition is set to explained. Second, I bounded a remaining premise of the asserted retry-growth defect - whether the retained read state can outlive the process. Source trace: newRaft constructs the read state fresh (readOnly at raft.go:462, pendingReadIndexMessages as a nil struct field at raft.go:430-435), the only mutations are the append in stepLeader and the swap in releasePendingReadIndexMessages, and the Storage interface exposes no read-state field at all (storage.go:48-95, and no ReadState/readStates reference exists in storage.go or raftpb). A restarted node therefore starts with an empty queue and empty ack map, so the accumulation is bounded by process lifetime. That narrows severity without weakening the claim: within a lifetime the library still imposes no bound and reclaims nothing.

knowledge.statement: The read state that a leader accumulates is volatile and cannot outlive the process. newRaft builds it fresh (readOnly via newReadOnly at raft.go:462; pendingReadIndexMessages is a slice field of the raft struct, raft.go:430-435, left nil), the only writers are the stepLeader MsgReadIndex append and the release path that swaps the slice out, and the Storage interface exposes only InitialState, Entries, Term, FirstIndex, LastIndex and Snapshot (storage.go:48-95) with no read-state member; there is no ReadState or readStates reference in storage.go or raftpb. A restarted node therefore begins with an empty pending queue and an empty ack map, so any accumulation is bounded by the process lifetime and cleared incidentally by a restart, even though the library never clears it while running.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to both StartNode and RestartNode paths, since both build the raft through newRaft; the statement is about library-side state only and says nothing about how a restart interacts with the caller's retries. It bounds the retry-growth finding rather than contradicting it: within one process lifetime there is still no bound and no reclamation.

interpretations.rationale: Addendum to the final measured revision of this question; the receipt, indices and claim are unchanged (receipt 6eccd9a311b84ba4b6c02771f746dd50, decisive indices 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 9 and 11, all comparisons complete and holding). What this revision adds is one bounded premise the account had not settled: whether the accumulated read state can persist beyond the process. It cannot. newRaft builds the read state fresh - readOnly is created by newReadOnly and pendingReadIndexMessages is a nil slice field of the raft struct - the only mutations are the append in stepLeader and the release path that swaps the slice out, and the Storage interface has no read-state member, with no ReadState or readStates reference anywhere in storage.go or raftpb. So a restart drops the queue and the ack map, and the operator has an incidental remedy (restart) even though the library never reclaims the state while running. I state this as a bound on severity, not as a defence of the behaviour: within a process lifetime the asserted defect stands unchanged - no library-side limit on accepted read requests, no reclamation of the queue (raft.reset leaves pendingReadIndexMessages in place, and only a quorum ack advances maybeAdvance for admitted requests), retained caller payload equal to accepted requests times context size, and one heartbeat per accepted request plus a burst on release. The claim's other boundaries are as previously recorded: unlimited growth requires CheckQuorum false (the library default, not required by ReadOnlySafe), with CheckQuorum true the window closes at step-down while the accumulated state is retained, the triggers were modelled rather than exercised over a network, and total process footprint, an OOM threshold, transport saturation and any liveness failure remain unmeasured and unclaimed.

knowledge.assertion: the accumulated read state is process-local and therefore cleared by a restart, which bounds but does not remove the defect
retained payload equals accepted requests times caller-chosen context size, held in distinct buffers
without CheckQuorum the queued path accumulates one entry per request and is not reclaimed while the process runs

limitations: Severity is measured for the retained caller payload only; total process footprint, allocator overhead, an OOM threshold, transport saturation and liveness failure are not claimed.
The accumulation is bounded by process lifetime because the state is not persisted, so a restart clears it incidentally; this bounds severity but is not a library-side reclamation mechanism.

All experiments drive direct raft instances with no responses delivered, so the triggers (partition from quorum with CheckQuorum false; quorum loss with CheckQuorum true) are modelled rather than exercised over a network.
etcd's own retry policy and RequestCtx sizes were not examined, so the practical magnitude in the primary downstream user is unknown.

The growth, drain and control cases each use one configuration at one depth (64 or 24 requests); linearity in the accepted-request count follows from the mechanism and from the byte measurement at one depth, not from a sweep of depths.

The control fixes the retry rate at eight per tick, so it shows the window closing within the election timeout but does not measure how much state a faster retry rate could accumulate in that interval.
